conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: However, the collections here are extremely rare, involving secret archives from various countries that should have been sealed away forever.

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: The mountains and soil listen to your wishes; regardless of what karma and retribution may be, fate already slumbers in your palm.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: This environment is really quite bizarre, but perhaps this is the atmosphere they intended to create.

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: The mountains and soil listen to your wishes; regardless of what karma and retribution may be, fate already slumbers in your palm.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Coming down, coming down.

conversation.speaker: player1

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Gray noticed two exhibits are intricately connected to your investigation.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Share your findings with your colleagues.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Great, now we can prove the old man has been swapped."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "There are other gains. I just went to the second floor. The windows there are opaque, relying entirely on artificial lighting. Haddin choosing the freight elevator to go upstairs might be to head to the control room to cut the lights, preventing Heim from casting spatial magic."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Whether we can leave records or secure the exhibits would be a great help to us, but unfortunately, it's quite difficult in practice.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "This guy is really a peculiar person."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Also, the Old World Black Book probably isn't easy to obtain; it's kept near Manson by magic."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David checks around to see if there's any sign prohibiting photography.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: It's pitch dark here, obviously to reduce light damage to the exhibits. Your request is naturally refused.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "The only good news is we snatched the Goloi Blessing."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Is it too late to learn now?"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: You've finished touring the museum's first floor, and the second floor is currently being set up. The clock points to 10 o'clock.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Four more hours. What can we do now, friends?"

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "I need to think; the current situation is a bit tricky." Feeling the situation is very tricky, with some leads but not many.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "It's not good to act rashly here, and we also know nothing about Haddin's specific plan."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Haddin's plan is probably to invade the control room via the freight elevator, turn off the lights, and then kill Heim."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Looks like we have to keep an eye on Haddin while also stopping the cousins."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Heim has a powerful attack magic released by sight and a passive defensive magic."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Let's go out for lunch first, chat while we eat."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Haddin's assassination plan probably won't succeed because of this; bullets aren't much use."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Perhaps we can prepare something, try not to let him see it."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: Planning to find a place to eat near the art gallery.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Stuff it into whom?"

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "How about we shove it to Haddin..."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Or we could stuff Haddin's soul into Gurevich's body?"

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Is there a chance to disguise as maintenance workers to get in?"

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Theoretically, our fallback plan is to find Haddin and provide remote assistance, like transferring his soul into Gurevich's body, but without directly intervening. Grab the Old World Black Book and run. With the recall spell and the archives, it should be enough to clear our names."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Then the problem becomes how we get that book."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "This is the best-case scenario. The worst case is we might be forced to intervene, then we'd have to face a tricky problem: how to withdraw."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Haddin still has to approach the building from the street, right!"

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "We don't know Manson's details either. But if he's going to display the Old World Black Book on site, then he'll definitely have to take it out. Under normal circumstances, we might also learn that spell."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Hopefully Haddin has already learned it..."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Yes, hopefully our eyesight is good enough."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "The best-case scenario is, Haddin wants to use the Thule Traditional Society to create chaos and then get in. We could also seize the opportunity."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: That's hoping for a bit too much. This world doesn't seem like the type to kindly respond to people's expectations.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "But that would be too boring, wouldn't it? And not secure enough—after all, we're not the only ones who want this book. Most likely, there won't be a chance to carefully peruse it."

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: The story Algorithm of the Heart recording has continued, currently 6636 texts recorded.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "I suggest we go find Manson first. We can disguise as journalists to get into the VIP room."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Folks, our cover identities are high-level intellectuals. I think making some meeting requests is reasonable. Disguising as journalists is also a good method."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "And it has to be when Manson and Gurevich are separate... They might not get along well anyway."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "That's a good idea... and we might even have a chance to ask the reporter lady for help."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Miss Gray is right."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Please note, the museum will temporarily close in 1 hour, at noon 12:00. Audience admission for the afternoon debate will begin at 13:30. Please be mindful of the time."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Alright, Alison, you go out later and tell the reporter that Haddin will appear in the afternoon. Then prepare the magic. Come in at the normal time in the afternoon."

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: Let me see, you're quite skilled at many things.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "If possible, you can come in with the reporter lady."

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: Let me see, you're quite skilled at many things.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "I'll try to stay behind and find an opportunity to contact Manson in advance."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "I wonder if we could call Manson first..."

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: Let me see, you're quite skilled at many things.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "If he hasn't left yet, he might be interested in our proposal."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Manson should arrive early to prepare, but I think Gurevich will come around the same time."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "No time to waste. I'll go out now to contact the reporter lady and prepare the Goloi Blessing spell. You all be careful."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Alright, you be careful too."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Alison leaves the museum, returns to the car to prepare spells, then finds a phone booth to call the journalist.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Do you have Manson's contact information? If you do, it would save us a lot of trouble."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "What if the journalist knows? Such a big shot might be acquiring artifacts somewhere."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Maybe the cousin has it, but unfortunately, he's not on our side."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Stop thinking about these irrelevant things, hurry up and find a suitable place to hide."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: @player4 You dial the number.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: Pretend to go to the first-floor restroom to use the toilet, observe if there are any suitable hiding spots inside.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Hello?" A professional woman's efficient voice comes from the other end of the line.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David also takes advantage of the museum still being open to look around for places to hide.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Miss Margaret, it's me, Alison." Alison lowers her voice. "We have news about Haddin. He's involved in a complex vortex and is about to confront Nazi remnants who wield black magic."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "You... what? Mr. Haddin is still alive? That's wonderful! And you—you're going to face who? Nazi remnants? And what... black magic?" She lowers her voice, her tone shifting from surprise to alarm. "Alison, are you insane? Do you know what you're saying?" "Are you asking for my help, or trying to drag me into... this madman's game?"

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Haddin probably has a death wish to stop the Nazi remnants. What we need to do aligns with his interests, so we want to contact the Nazi's target in advance to give him a warning. Of course, we won't put you in danger personally, but your identity as a journalist might be able to help." Alison hesitates as she finishes.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "What do you want me to do?"

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Borrow your journalist identity to conduct an interview in the VIP room; we want to make contact with the target. As for you, you can wait on the periphery for an opportunity to gather news material." "There might be a big commotion. You'll be relatively safe gathering news from the periphery, and Haddin will be there too. This might be... the last chance to see him. You could also get some information from him."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Huh? What? Why would you think having a journalist's ID means the VIP will accept an interview? Is a press pass some kind of golden ticket? I've been turned away plenty of times." "If people just accepted interviews because you're a journalist, this job would be way too easy."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "We're just grasping at every possible opportunity," Alison says with a bitter smile. "Even if you can't get in, it's good for you to be a witness here. Just from a professional journalist's perspective, I don't think you'd want to miss this story." "This is just an invitation; the decision is yours."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "You're right," she says softly, her voice like a hidden breeze—light, but not weak. "Of course I don't want to miss this story. Nazi remnants, black magic, federal police, mysterious disappearances... If I were the Margaret from ten years ago, obsessed with the Pulitzer, I'd have snatched the clues from your hands and charged in by now." "But now I know that the truly valuable stories are often the ones you can't write. Like Haddin, like what you're about to do... They won't make the front page or the evening news. Because they're too dangerous, and too real."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Alright, I understand. In any case, thank you for the help you provided earlier," Alison replies after a moment of silence.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "But who am I kidding? Deep down, I'm still driven by curiosity for the truth. Even if it can't be published, I want to know what's hidden behind it..." "Where should we meet?"

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "You really gave me a scare with that dramatic pause. Is that a professional habit for journalists, to surprise the audience?" Alison lets out a long sigh. "Everything will happen at the art gallery. I'll wait for you at the entrance."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "I'm used to saving the bombshell for the end. See you soon."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Hangs up the phone, Alison returns to the car and tosses the cube into the mirror.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "This doesn't look like a good place to hide." Feeling the restroom isn't a very suitable hiding place, leaves dejectedly.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: A spot closer to the VIP room is best, so we don't get caught by security before we even make it to the meeting...

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: You want to hide, but there really aren't many good hiding places in the museum. Besides the exhibition halls, there are only restrooms or staff-only areas marked 'No Entry for Visitors'.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Andrew calmly paced back and forth in the museum, observing the personnel deployment and situation.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David also pretended to admire the exhibits while strolling around.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: Unable to find a good hiding spot, he reluctantly left.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David left just before the museum closed.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: These suited security guards are clearly not the kind of 500-mark-a-month, idle neighborhood watchmen.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Alison approached her, "Over here!"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Huh?" She seemed surprised but quickly regained her composure. "Oh right, you're in disguise."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Briefly explain the situation to Margaret using the art gallery's posted posters.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "So what is Mr. Haddin's plan?"

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "He has a grudge against that Nazi... he might want to settle it today." Alison hesitated, not telling her about discovering Haddin's body. "We found Haddin's hideout; he left behind a timed plan diagram."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "No, I don't think it's that simple. According to you, Mr. Haddin has some understanding of black magic?"

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Yes, Haddin likely conducted considerable research for revenge."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Haddin is taking action personally?" she repeated softly, her gaze sharpening. "He and that Nazi... have a grudge." She murmured, as if weighing the word's significance. "Then he must have thought it through carefully. Haddin isn't an emotional man; even with anger in his heart, he would rehearse, revise, and reenact every detail over and over before acting, until he was sure he had at least an eighty percent chance of success."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "...We truly don't know him that well. Since you say so, his plan must be far more meticulous than we imagined." Alison pondered for a moment.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Her voice rose slightly: "What he couldn't anticipate are 'variables outside himself'—like you, like third parties who shouldn't have appeared, like unexpected delays, even a temporarily reassigned guard. These are what's truly fatal."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "So you mean... we should help him deal with these unstable factors."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: She paused: "As long as you can do that... he can win."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "We'll try. Unfortunately, we don't know the specific, detailed plan." Alison nodded.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "What about your companions? It's not just you, is it...."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "The three of them are inside, trying to find hiding spots to gain the upper hand. The art gallery won't reopen until 1:30 PM. There's heavy security both inside and out, likely influenced by the organization behind this."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Is it possible it's simply because these artifacts are very valuable..."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "I don't know if Haddin accounted for this in his plan."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Max Manson places great importance on his collection and has specifically hired multiple private security firms for it."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "So Manson hired the security."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: After talking for a while, an announcement urging visitors to leave echoed from inside the museum, as preparations for the afternoon debate were starting early.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: Reluctantly left the venue, shaking heads and sighing as they walked out.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David exited with the departing visitors and joined Gray and the reporter.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Andrew didn't gain much; now he could only wait for an opportunity to act.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Alison waved to them.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Hello? Which one of you is Mr. player3?"

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Good afternoon, Miss Margaret, it's Henry Wilson now." David greeted her.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: Nodded and stepped forward to shake hands, "We are immensely grateful for your invaluable assistance."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "During these days of our trip to Germany, you have been practically our only friend—brave, intelligent, and full of a sense of justice."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Journalists like you are rare these days; the rest have either become shameless mouthpieces and hounds for politicians or turned into madams peddling gossip and fake news."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Haha, you flatter me too much. I've merely held onto the original intent of a journalism professional."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Miss Margaret has provided us with some new information and clues," Alison shared with her colleagues.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David listened and nodded repeatedly.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "What do you think? This information is quite valuable for reference."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "We do need to eliminate some unstable factors to prevent Haddin's failure. After all, we need him alive."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "I see. It seems Miss Margaret understands Haddin better than we do." Began to ponder, "Then perhaps we should also share the information and plans we've gathered so far."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Let's grab a quick bite nearby and talk over lunch? The venue probably won't open for entry until half past one."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Of course."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Great, great, it's our treat."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Perfect, we were thinking the same. Any recommended places?"

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "We currently have evidence that Gurevich, Brandt, and Rilke have each been possessed by some Nazi remnant—though it sounds bizarre, it's true."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Let's keep it simple for now. Once this is over, we'll treat Haddin to a big meal together."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: You ate at a nearby restaurant called Old Roman. A meal without appetizers, wine, dessert, or coffee—a bit shabby for treating guests.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "We believe Heim—the Nazi mage possessing Gurevich's body—intends to seize or destroy that collection, while Haddin's goal is likely to kill Heim. Our original plan was to contact Manson before the speech, warn him about Gurevich, and have him teach us the incantation. If possible, we'd also meet with Haddin in advance to exchange intelligence."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Why do you think you could recognize Haddin? He will definitely be disguised, and why would he trust strangers on sight?" Margaret frowned.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Sounds like we were about to execute a flawed plan. Good thing we have your help."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: Nodded, "You make a valid point. In such a short time, he certainly couldn't trust us. But we're worried that coordinating after Haddin makes his move might be too late—Heim himself is a powerful mage, and other forces also want him dead."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Why don't you think about who else is currently interested in Haddin?"

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Ahem, it's the Americans."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "The Americans?" Margaret looked puzzled.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Also, the security here is extremely tight. We haven't found a good way to bypass it—perhaps we can only hope Haddin has some method to handle it."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "When they investigated, they found Americans had put a bounty on Haddin's head, demanding he be killed on the spot today."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Then we must take out these Americans?" Margaret made an exaggerated throat-slitting gesture.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Huh? No, no, no, no, no." David quickly shook his head.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "That shouldn't be necessary. We just need to try and divert their attention for him."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "What? The Americans have already tracked him here?"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Well, do you have any weapons with you?"

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David nodded, indicating there was no need to worry about that; everyone was well-armed.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "We have some necessary firepower, but entering the art gallery requires going through security."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "In principle, we'd better not engage in direct firefights with them." He shrugged after speaking. "But when chaos breaks out, who knows who's on which side?"

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "How do journalists hide the things they carry during undercover investigations?"

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Hmm... we usually don't carry such large items; at most, we hide a voice recorder in the collar."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Looking at it this way, we still have to wait for an opportunity."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "We have those too, but unfortunately, a voice recorder doesn't have much stopping power when smashed against someone's head."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "But opportunities don't wait for people; we'll have to improvise on the spot."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "But I have a special transport case for camera equipment in my car."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Excellent! This way we can bring some things in."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "You're practically an angel sent by God to save us! Hiding bombs like this should be no problem, but the gun bodies might be tricky."

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: Let me see, you're quite skilled in many things.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Let's talk about what we can see right now. Do you think the Thule Traditional Society's gathering here is part of Haddin's plan?"

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Yes, he arranged to send something to the Thule Society this afternoon."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Then we don't need to deal with those guys for him. What we need to watch out for are the Americans and..."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Alright, then I think what we can do is prevent the Americans and the Freikorps from interfering."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Sigh... not knowing your dance partner's steps, yet having to coordinate with them for this dance, it's really difficult."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Actually, there's also that thing.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Also, I'm very sorry, but we cannot enter as a single group. Please understand, as I still have to live in this city."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Andrew thought to himself, that thing specifically designed to kill time travelers, if that thing is real.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "Now we just need to figure out how to get the pistols inside. Can they fit in the equipment case?"

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Your guidance is already the greatest help to us. Otherwise, our original plan might have ruined everything."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "You should be able to disassemble the guns and place them in the compartments of the transport case."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "We are extremely grateful."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "This is already a tremendous help. Without you, we'd truly be jumping into a fire pit."

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "After eating, let's go prepare the things."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Roughly how many guns can it hold? I'd also like to bring smoke grenades inside."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "Adding two smoke grenades shouldn't be a problem."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Then how do we withdraw and wrap things up..."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Alright. Be sure to stay safe, Miss Margaret."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: "To be honest, I've already stopped thinking about completing the mission alive." David shrugged. "Take it one step at a time. Maybe by then, everything will already be in complete chaos."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "If that doesn't work, we'll have to rely on smoke grenades or something to create chaos and seize the chance to leave."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "Well, whatever..." Andrew chewed more slowly.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David had already memorized the art gallery's floor plan. He felt he had done all he could; the rest was up to God.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Oh, by the way, little Andrew is also a good cook. Let him prepare a proper big meal for us later."

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: After setting your flags, you disassembled the guns in the car and packed them into the hidden compartment of Margaret's equipment transport case, waiting only for the moment the museum opens.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: According to the previous plan, David enters the art gallery without weapons, turns on the button microphone, hoping it can record some possible evidence.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: The Thule Traditional Society, that neo-Nazi group, is still chanting slogans, but after enduring the midday sun, their momentum seems listless compared to the morning.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Hopefully, they can still serve the purpose Haddin intended.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: After entering the gallery, Alison scans the security situation once more, focusing on the security passage area.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Andrew pokes his head around, preparing to locate Manson. Manson has put great effort into security; this likely won't be easy.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: Margaret maintains some distance from you and goes through security first. "Camera... the compartment has film, can't be exposed to sunlight... yes... this is my press pass... thank you."

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Follow the guidance and go up to the second floor first to check the situation.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Andrew prepares to listen carefully to the debate.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David also goes up to the second floor. For now, the best approach is to wait and see.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Not only can we watch a magician and a psychologist debate, but also a pistol debate. Andrew is full of enthusiasm.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: The number of security personnel on the museum's second floor has greatly increased. Numerous guards form two human walls, isolating the audience from the guests and staff, creating a limited, enclosed area.

conversation.speaker: player1
conversation.text: <player2> rolled d3=2

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Andrew follows his older brother and sister, ready to follow their arrangements. Of course, he's also looking for a good spot for himself.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: David observes the audience seating, looking for a seat closest to the control panel and farthest from the security guards, then sits down.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: Sit in a position near the control panel. Observe the VIP section and audience seating. Are there any noteworthy individuals?

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: There's no such contradictory requirement.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: Thrown off by this grand setup, try to get close to Margaret, using your body to block the line of sight towards her, making it easier for teammates to retrieve the goods.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: The control panel is under the supervision of security.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Well, never mind then.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Sitting in a row, sharing the fruits. Andrew isn't confident in his shooting skills, so he gives the better shooting positions to others.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: You all choose front-row seats. Margaret pretends to assemble photography equipment nearby, secretly handing over your guns and C4 to you.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: Sitting obediently beside player5, his eyes constantly and curiously scan the area behind the security guard... and occasionally glance sideways at the freight elevator.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: Quietly assembling the pistol, checking the watch after preparation is complete.
